WWAggr and naive aggregations of ensemble scores

Source: R/dfr_wwaggr.R
wwaggr.Rd

Aggregates the change point scores of the members of an ensemble (cpd_scores() of a cpd_ensemble()) into one score per time step. WWAggr (Stepikin et al., 2025) compares, at every step, the scores of all members in a "future" window of the last window_size steps with those in an anchor ("history") window, by the Wasserstein distance of the two samples (the window flattened over steps and members) or by the maximum mean discrepancy; the naive aggregations take the mean, minimum, maximum, median or a quantile of the members at every step.

Usage

wwaggr(
  scores,
  method = c("wasserstein", "mmd", "mean", "min", "max", "median", "quantile"),
  window_size = 3,
  anchor = c("prev", "start", "combined"),
  p = 1,
  kernel = c("rbf", "multiscale"),
  bandwidth = NULL,
  q = 0.5
)

Arguments

scores

Scores of the members: an array [member, sequence, time] or a matrix [member, time] (one sequence).

method

"wasserstein" (WWAggr, default), "mmd", "mean", "min", "max", "median" or "quantile".

window_size

Size of the windows (distance methods).

anchor

Anchor window: "prev" (default, the window_size steps before the future window, as Algorithm 1 of the paper), "start" (the first window_size steps of the sequence) or "combined" (the first window_size %/% 2 steps followed by the window_size %/% 2 steps before the last ones; the future window then has 2 * (window_size %/% 2) steps).

p

Order of the Wasserstein distance.

kernel

Kernel of the MMD: "rbf" or "multiscale".

bandwidth

Bandwidths of the MMD kernel. NULL uses those of the reference: 10, 15, 20 and 50 (rbf) or 0.2, 0.5, 0.9 and 1.3 (multiscale).

q

Quantile of the "quantile" method (the median is 0.5, the minimum 0 and the maximum 1; linear interpolation as torch.quantile).

Value

A matrix [sequence, time] of aggregated scores, or a vector for one sequence.

Details

The steps where some member has no score (the first steps of the representation models) are left out, as in the reference code, and get NA. For the distance methods, the score of the i-th remaining step (i > window_size) compares the future window of steps i - window_size to i - 1 with the anchor window, and the first window_size scores are 0 (anchor_window_detector_batch of the reference, src/ensembles/ distances.py). For "prev", the anchor starts at max(1, i - 2 * window_size).

The 1-Wasserstein distance of two samples of the same size is the mean absolute difference of their order statistics, and the p-Wasserstein distance the p-th root of the mean of their p-th powers. The MMD treats the steps of a window as samples and the members as dimensions; it is the mean of k(x, x') + k(y, y') - 2 k(x, y') over all pairs, with the sum of the kernels of all bandwidths: exp(-d / (2 a)) (rbf) or a^2 / (a^2 + d) (multiscale), d the squared distance. With calibrated members, the scores are in [0, 1] and so is the 1-Wasserstein distance, so that a threshold around 0.5 works without tuning (Section IV of the paper).

References

Stepikin, A., Romanenkova, E. and Zaytsev, A. (2025). WWAggr: A window Wasserstein-based aggregation for ensemble change point detection. 2025 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM), 1535-1544. doi:10.1109/ICDM65498.2025.00163

Examples

set.seed(1)
# 10 members, 2 sequences of 30 steps; the change is at step 16.
scores <- array(stats::runif(10 * 2 * 30, 0, 0.2), c(10, 2, 30))
scores[, , 16:30] <- scores[, , 16:30] + 0.7
round(wwaggr(scores, window_size = 3)[1, 12:22], 2)
#>  [1] 0.01 0.01 0.02 0.01 0.01 0.23 0.47 0.73 0.50 0.24 0.01
round(wwaggr(scores, method = "mean")[1, 12:22], 2)
#>  [1] 0.09 0.09 0.09 0.06 0.79 0.84 0.80 0.80 0.82 0.83 0.80
